subject: HealthScope — model fit & safety evals follow-up
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@healthscope.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + next steps from today’s model fit call

Thanks again for the demo this morning — really helpful context. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can get an internal approval to proceed with evaluations:

- Goal: reduce triage time in support KB search by surfacing concise, policy-compliant suggestions for agents. Sensitive content (PHI) appears ~8% of queries.
- Priority success criteria: answer accuracy >= 85% on our internal prompts, refusal rate consistent with our policy (low false positives), latency < 300ms p95 for single-turn queries.

Ask: can Redwood run a small model-fit evaluation on our prompt set (attached) and recommend 2–3 candidate models/configs (including quantization tradeoffs)? We’d also like a short safety/refusal evaluation focusing on PHI/medical advice and guardrail prompt examples.

Attaching the prompt set and a sample transcript. Happy to align on acceptance criteria — Tom and I are available next Wed for a quick sync.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product
HealthScope

Attachment: healthscope_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt set, 120 rows)
Attachment: healthscope_sample_transcript.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today’s model fit call

Hi Alyssa — great speaking with you and Tom. Appreciate the prompt set and sample transcript. Next steps from our side (summary + timeline):

1) Quick discovery validation (24–48h): Rafael and I will sanity-check the prompt set and map prompts to evaluation buckets (factual retrieval, policy-sensitive, conversational clarification).
2) Candidate selection & perf benchmarks (3 business days): we’ll run the prompt set across 3 candidate model configurations and return a small benchmark report (accuracy, latency, token cost).
3) Safety/refusal behavior eval (3 business days, runs in parallel): short suite that includes PHI redaction, medical-advice refusal, and guardrail prompts. We’ll include examples for refusal templates.

Initial recommended candidates (based on our hosted catalog + latency/cost balance):
- redwood-rlhf-3b-quant (good latency, lower cost; watch for calibration on refusals)
- redwood-instruct-7b (strong instruction-following; moderate latency)
- open-llama-13b-8bit (highest quality on retrieval but higher resource needs)

I’ve uploaded the benchmark scaffold and an initial model-run PDF with placeholder results here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HealthScopeEval (link also below). I’m attaching the prompt set back with mapping and our benchmark PDF for transparency.

Questions for you:
- Do you have any hard rejection criteria for refusal behavior (examples we should treat as non-negotiable)?
- Is it acceptable for us to run tests on hosted/non-dedicated capacity (we’ll mark data as not retained in the scoring cluster), or do you require a Private deployment for the evals?

We’ll start checks tomorrow and aim to have a candid model comparison + safety summary by end of week. We’ll also propose guardrail prompt templates you can drop into your in-product policy layer.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark_results_candidate_models.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@healthscope.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today’s model fit call

Quick technical note from the infra side — thanks for the prompt set, Alyssa. A few items we’ll cover in the evaluation:

- Safety/regression guardrails: we’ll include a refusal calibration test and a policy-behavior matrix. For PHI we run specific redaction/obfuscation checks and a simulated prompt-injection suite (we’ll show failure modes).
- Regression monitoring: as we evaluate quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit), we’ll track per-prompt quality delta vs. the FP32 baseline and highlight any prompts with >5% degradation.
- Data handling: for hosted runs we use ephemeral scoring clusters (no retention) and provide MD5 checksums of inputs/outputs for audit. If you need a private run, we can arrange a short Dedicated window — that will affect timing by ~1–2 days.

Proposed concrete deliverables for the report:
- CSV with per-prompt pass/fail and metrics (accuracy, refusal, latency)
- Top-line PDF summary with recommended model + config and cost estimates
- Safety matrix and guardrail prompt templates (.csv + examples in the PDF)
- Short recording of failure cases (screenshare snippets)

We’ll kick off the runs this morning. Marissa — tagging you for the acceptance-criteria question from Alyssa. Alyssa/Tom — any additional test cases we should add (e.g., borderline PHI vs clear PHI)?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
ML Infrastructure Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachment: safety_eval_summary.xlsx

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@healthscope.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today’s model fit call

Perfect — that plan works for us. A couple quick clarifications:

- Acceptance: we’ll mark a prompt as acceptable if accuracy >= 85% AND refusal behavior matches our policy on all PHI tests. For borderline PHI we expect the model to ask clarifying questions rather than hallucinate.
- Environment: hosted ephemeral runs are fine for the evals. If results look promising we’ll request a Dedicated proof-of-concept for a week prior to contract.

Tom and I are available for a 30-min sync on Thu 9/3 at 10:00 AM PT if you want to walk through early results. Otherwise we’ll wait for the report later this week.

Thanks — looking forward to the summary and guardrail templates.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Product, HealthScope
